title: Kasseien and Bergs, A Week in the Flemish Ardennes

bestPeriod.note: Ride in April for Ronde van Vlaanderen atmosphere, September for dry cobbles and empty lanes; winter turns the kasseien into ice.

summary: Six days of short brutal cobbled climbs from a single Oudenaarde base, linked by Flanders' knooppunten network and the Ronde van Vlaanderen route.
hook: Nothing here is more than 150 metres above sea level, and that is the joke. The Flemish Ardennes hide their difficulty in 400-metre ramps of granite setts pitched at 20 per cent, strung together by lanes so narrow two cars cannot pass. You will ride 400 km in a week and climb more than you expect, and you will do it all from one hotel in Oudenaarde.

snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: 380-430 km, approx 5,500 m cumulative gain; asphalt lanes with roughly 35 km of cobbled sectors (kasseien) split between climbs and flat sections
snapshot.Getting There: Brussels (BRU) → train to Brussel-Zuid/Bruxelles-Midi, then IC to Oudenaarde (approx 1h from Brussels, hourly)
snapshot.Who It Suits: Road cyclists who want short savage climbs rather than long ones, and anyone who has watched the Ronde on television for a decade

itinerary.title: Arrival, Koppenberg reconnaissance
itinerary.morning: Train in to Oudenaarde. The station has a Fietspunt, Flanders' network of station bike points, staffed by social-economy operators, where you can leave a bike box, and a Blue-bike rack for a cheap city hack bike. Build up, check the tyre pressure and drop it: 5.5-6 bar on 28 mm tyres is the local orthodoxy on cobbles, not the 7 bar you ride at home.
itinerary.afternoon: A short shakedown loop east to Melden and the Koppenberg. It is 600 metres long, averages 11.6 per cent and hits 22 per cent at the bend, the single hardest ramp in Flanders, and unrideable if you are boxed in behind someone who stalls. Ride it once, badly, then again.
itinerary.evening: The Centrum Ronde van Vlaanderen on the Markt has the race's archive, a cobble-simulator and a café that pours Kwaremont blond. Entry approx €10.
itinerary.dayStats: 38 km, +480 m, asphalt with 1.1 km of cobbles (Koppenberg, Mariaborrestraat).

itinerary.title: The Ronde finale, in order
itinerary.morning: Ride the closing sequence of the modern Tour of Flanders as the race does it. South to Kluisbergen, then the Oude Kwaremont: 2,200 m long, 1,500 m of it cobbled, averaging 4 per cent with an 11.6 per cent opening ramp through the hamlet.
itinerary.afternoon: Straight on to the Paterberg, 360 m, averaging 12.9 per cent, maxing at 20.3, then loop and repeat both, which is what the race does. Finish over the Koppenberg and Steenbeekdries, and take the Mariaborrestraat descent slowly; it is cobbled and off-camber.
itinerary.evening: Back to Oudenaarde along the Schelde towpath, which is smooth asphalt and a relief. Eat at one of the Markt brasseries; the local beer is Adriaen Brouwer, brewed in the town by Roman.

itinerary.title: Geraardsbergen and the Muur
itinerary.morning: East across the Zwalm valley on knooppunten, the numbered node network that covers all of Flanders. Ride node to node rather than by GPS trace; the signs are green-on-white and never more than 2 km apart.
itinerary.afternoon: The Muur van Geraardsbergen: 1,075 m of cobbles through the town and up through the beech woods to the Kapelmuur, averaging 9.3 per cent with a 19.8 per cent section at the Chapel bend. Follow it with the Bosberg, 980 m at 5.8 per cent, which is the polite one.
itinerary.evening: Geraardsbergen makes mattentaart, a curdled-milk tart with EU protected status. Buy two at a bakery on the Markt and eat one immediately.

itinerary.title: The flat cobbles: Paddestraat and Haaghoek
itinerary.morning: A deliberately different day. Ride north-east through Zottegem to the Paddestraat at Velzeke, 2,300 metres of dead-flat protected historic cobbles, and a completely different skill from climbing them. Big gear, high cadence, hands light on the tops.
itinerary.afternoon: Link to the Haaghoek at Brakel, another 2,000 m of flat setts, then take the Leberg and Berendries (940 m at 7 per cent) on the way home. This is the day your wrists learn something.
itinerary.evening: Rest the hands. The Ename abbey ruins and archaeological park sit 3 km from Oudenaarde on the Schelde and are free to walk.
itinerary.dayStats: 85 km, +780 m, approx 7 km cobbles, almost all flat.

itinerary.title: Recovery on the Schelde and the Kluisbos
itinerary.morning: A genuine easy day. Follow the Schelde towpath south on smooth asphalt toward Kerkhove and Avelgem, then cross into Hainaut for coffee.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb the Kluisberg on its asphalt side to Mont-de-l'Enclus, the wooded ridge that marks the language border, and descend the Knokteberg. Total climbing under 500 m.
itinerary.evening: Oudenaarde's Adriaan Brouwer brewery tap and the Tacambaroplein terraces. Early night.
itinerary.dayStats: 62 km, +460 m, asphalt with 600 m of cobbles (Kluisberg lower section).

itinerary.title: The northern bergs and the Hotond ridge
itinerary.morning: North-west over the Eikenberg (1,200 m of cobbles at 5.2 per cent) and the Taaienberg, 530 m at 6.6 per cent with a 15.8 per cent kick, Tom Boonen's hill, and the one with the best surface.
itinerary.afternoon: Up onto the Hotondberg, at 150 m the high point of East Flanders, then the Kanarieberg (1,000 m at 7.7 per cent) and the Kruisberg into Ronse. On a clear day you can see the cooling towers at Doel from the Hotond ridge.
itinerary.evening: Ronse has a Flemish-French bilingual edge and a good Saturday market. Ride the last 12 km home in the low light along the Molenbeek.

itinerary.title: The Ronde sportive loop, short version
itinerary.morning: Whatever hurt most, ride it again. The standard local farewell loop is Oude Kwaremont-Paterberg-Koppenberg-Steenbeekdries-Taaienberg, roughly 55 km from Oudenaarde.
itinerary.afternoon: Wash the bike at the hotel bay, pack it, and take a late train. Bikes on NMBS require a bike supplement, roughly €4-8 depending on the ticket, and are barred from some Brussels-bound peak services on weekday mornings and evenings.
itinerary.evening: If your flight is next morning, sleep near Brussel-Zuid rather than at the airport; the bike carriage there is simpler.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Leopold
accommodationStrategy.description: Directly on the Markt, opposite the Ronde centre, with a locked bike room off the courtyard and staff who have handled cyclists for decades. Every one of the seven rides starts from the front door, which removes the daily car shuffle that ruins most cobble trips.
accommodationStrategy.booking: four months ahead, and immediately if your week touches the Ronde van Vlaanderen weekend in early April.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €110-150 per night for two with breakfast

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel De Rantere
accommodationStrategy.description: Quieter, on the Schelde a few hundred metres from the centre, with private parking and a ground-floor storage room. Its restaurant serves at a proper hour for people who come back at 19:00 covered in Flemish clay, which the Markt brasseries do not always do.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Steenhuyse
accommodationStrategy.style: Boutique rooms in a listed townhouse
accommodationStrategy.description: The upgrade: five suites in an eighteenth-century mansion on the square, with a secure interior courtyard for bikes. Worth it if you are two couples and want space to spread wet kit; not worth it if you need a workshop, which it does not have.

logistics.emergency: 112 for everything in Belgium. Ambulances reach the berg lanes slowly; give a knooppunt number, not a road name, when you call.
logistics.weather: Flanders is maritime and unstable. A 15 °C day with 30 km/h of westerly and rain is normal in April and will feel far colder on a 60 km/h descent.
logistics.money: Cards are universal. Village cafés close on Monday and Tuesday almost without exception; the Markt in Oudenaarde is the reliable fallback.

other.label: Knooppunten
other.text: The node network is the practical navigation layer. Buy the Vlaamse Ardennen fietsnetwerkkaart at the Oudenaarde tourist office, approx €8, and write the node sequence on bar tape. It is faster than a phone in rain.

other.label: Bikes on trains
other.text: NMBS charges a bike supplement of roughly €4 for a single journey and around €8 for a day, with no reservation and no guaranteed space. Bikes are restricted on weekday peak services into and out of Brussels, roughly 06:30-09:00 and 16:00-18:30. Folding bikes travel free.

other.label: Blue-bike and Fietspunt
other.text: Blue-bike rents from Oudenaarde station for a few euros a day for members; the Fietspunt does basic repairs and will store a bike box for the week. Neither rents road bikes, bring your own or hire from the Centrum Ronde van Vlaanderen, which keeps a fleet of road and e-road bikes at roughly €35-60 per day.

other.label: Luggage transfer
other.text: Deliberately not needed: one base for seven nights means nothing moves but you. The only transfer worth arranging is the bike box between Brussels Airport and Oudenaarde, which a local taxi will do for approx €120-150 each way, or which the train handles free if the box is on a folding trolley.

other.label: Cobble law
other.text: The historic sectors, Paddestraat, Haaghoek, the Muur, are protected monuments. Riding the smooth gutter is legal but locally frowned on and often full of gravel and glass.

proTips: Drop your tyre pressure by a full bar before the cobbled days and run 28-30 mm rubber. The single biggest cause of ruined trips here is a pinch flat on the Haaghoek.
Ride the Oude Kwaremont on the left-hand crown, not the centre. The crown is worn flatter and the gutter is where the punctures live.
Approach the Koppenberg with 200 m of clear road behind you and commit; there is no restarting once you stall on the 22 per cent bend.
On the Muur, the cobbles are worst in the town section and best above the treeline. Save something for the last 200 m to the Chapel.
Go to the Centrum Ronde van Vlaanderen on your first evening, not your last. Its route maps and the staff's advice on which sectors are currently resurfaced will change your week's planning.
Book Oudenaarde accommodation for the Ronde weekend a full year out, or ride the sportive on the Saturday and leave town before the professionals arrive.

packingNotes: Tyres of 28 mm minimum, tubeless if possible, plus two spare tubes and a tyre boot.
Double-wrapped bar tape or gel inserts under the tape. Wrists take more punishment here than legs.
Full mudguards or clip-ons, Flemish farm lanes stay wet for days after rain, and the mud is fine clay.
A packable rain jacket and a spare base layer in a jersey pocket; the temperature swing between a sheltered climb and an exposed ridge is real.
Overshoes and long-finger gloves even in May.
A paper knooppunten map in a waterproof sleeve.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Rain turns the cobbles greasy.** Wet setts on a 20 per cent gradient are close to unrideable on a road bike. Fallback: Day 4's flat-cobble plan and Day 5's asphalt loop can swap into any slot; the Schelde towpath always works.
**Peak-hour bike ban strands you at Brussel-Zuid.** Fallback: take an IC to Ghent Sint-Pieters instead and change there for Oudenaarde outside the restricted window, or ride the 30 km from Ghent.

**A broken derailleur hanger 40 km from base.** There is no bike shop in most of these villages. Fallback: carry a spare hanger and a quick link; failing that, the Fietspunt at Oudenaarde station does same-day basic work and De Lijn buses take bikes only on limited routes, so budget for a taxi.

**You overcook Day 2 and lose the week.** Five thousand metres of climbing in short violent efforts wrecks people who train on long climbs. Fallback: Day 5 is a real recovery day, use it, and cut Day 6's Kanarieberg if the legs are gone.
